failure_summary.description: Trajectories repeatedly returned no relevant hits (Hit@10=0) and the agent did not reliably broaden to repository-wide exact searches or try concise semantic synonyms after failing a subtree search.

Agent steps show repeated or empty search attempts — the skill guidance doesn't enforce using exact quoted tokens or constrained single-identifier queries, causing noisy or empty results and failure to read candidate files.

patch.reasoning: All three failures share the same root causes: (1) the agent did not consistently perform the single broaden-to-repo-wide exact search and try concise synonyms when subtree/index searches failed, and (2) searches were not constrained to exact discriminative tokens (quoted strings, CLI flags, configuration keys), causing empty or noisy results. The edits add an explicit, prescriptive search-and-fallback procedure and strengthen the failure-recovery guidance so agents follow a deterministic, minimal set of search steps (exact token -> repo-wide exact -> one concise synonym -> return NOT FOUND) and prefer narrow queries. This reduces repeated redundant exploration and increases evidence hits.

edits.content:
### Search and fallback procedure

- Always prefer one exact, discriminative token or quoted phrase per grep call (for example: an exact error message, CLI flag, config key, API name, or quoted heading). Avoid OR/regex expressions that return very large result sets.
- If you inspect a product subtree (via index.md) and an exact grep inside that subtree returns zero results, perform exactly one immediate broaden step: a repository-wide exact grep for the same token.
- If the repository-wide exact grep returns zero results, try exactly one concise semantic synonym or closely related documentation term (preserving product/feature constraints) and run a repository-wide exact grep for that synonym.
- If both repository-wide greps return zero results, stop and return NOT FOUND. Do not continue repeated subtree exploration or unconstrained searches.
- When a grep returns candidate files, open the best candidate with read and verify the surrounding heading and frontmatter before citing. Only cite passages visible in the read output as evidence.

edits.target: - If an index route is wrong, broaden once to repository-wide exact search instead of repeatedly exploring that subtree.
edits.content: - If an index route is wrong, broaden exactly once to a repository-wide exact search for the same discriminative token. If the repository-wide exact search yields no results, try exactly one concise semantic synonym (repository-wide exact grep). If that also yields no results, stop and return NOT FOUND. Do not repeatedly explore the same subtree or run multiple broad/fuzzy searches.
